\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter09.ImprovedFriedgut}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut parameter]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\leanok
For a real number $\eta$, define the improved Friedgut parameter by
$\rho(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut constant]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutConstant}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutConstant}
\leanok
For each real number $\eta$, define the improved Friedgut constant to be
$\left(\frac{2}{\eta}+1\right)^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of Rho]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_pos}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\eta>0$, the quantity $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper Bound for Rho]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_le_one}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\eta>0$, the quantity $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ satisfies
$\rho(\eta)\le 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict Upper Bound for Rho]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_lt_one}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_lt_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\eta>0$, the quantity $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ satisfies
$\rho(\eta)<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Friedgut Constant and Rho]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutConstant_eq_inv_rho_sq}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutConstant_eq_inv_rho_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFriedgutConstant, FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $\eta>0$, define $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ and
$C(\eta)=(2/\eta+1)^2$. Then $C(\eta)=\rho(\eta)^{-2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reciprocal identity for the improved parameter]
\lean{FABL.two_div_eta_add_one_eq_inv_improvedFriedgutRho}
\label{FABL.two_div_eta_add_one_eq_inv_improvedFriedgutRho}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFriedgutRho}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $\eta>0$, $2/\eta+1$ equals the reciprocal of $\eta/(2+\eta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut constant]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutGeneralConstant}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutGeneralConstant}
\leanok
For each real number $\eta$, define $C(\eta)$ by $C(0)=1$ and, when $\eta\ne 0$, by
$C(\eta)=\left(\frac{2}{\eta}+1\right)^{1+\eta}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[General Constant and Rho]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutGeneralConstant_eq_inv_rho_rpow}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutGeneralConstant_eq_inv_rho_rpow}

\difficulty{3}

$C(\eta)=(2/\eta+1)^{1+\eta}$. Then $C(\eta)=\rho(\eta)^{-(1+\eta)}$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.lowDegreeCoordinateMass_le_inv_rho_pow_mul_stableInfluence}
\label{FABL.lowDegreeCoordinateMass_le_inv_rho_pow_mul_stableInfluence}

\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $i$
be a coordinate, and let $k$ be a natural number. For any real $\rho$ with
$0<\rho\leq 1$, the low-degree coordinate mass of $f$ at $i$ through degree $k$ is at
most $\rho^{-k}$ times the stable influence of the real-valued version of $f$ at $i$
with parameter $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.stableInfluence_improvedFriedgutRho_le}

$\tau$, then its stable influence at parameter $\eta/(2+\eta)$, applied to the
real-valued version of $f$, is at most $\tau^{1/(1+\eta)}$ times the Boolean influence

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut threshold]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.improvedFriedgutRho, FABL.totalInfluence}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in
$\{−1,1\}$, and let $\epsilon,\eta\in\mathbb R$. Its improved Friedgut threshold is
$\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\rho(\eta)^k\right)^{1+\eta}$, where $I(f)$ is the total
influence of $f$ and $\rho(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the Threshold]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold_pos}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_pos, FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function.
Write $T(f)$ for the sum, over the $n$ coordinates, of the expected squared discrete
derivatives of $f$, and set $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ and
$\Theta(f,\epsilon,\eta,k)=(\frac{\epsilon}{T(f)}\rho(\eta)^k)^{1+\eta}$. If
$\epsilon>0$, $\eta>0$, $k$ is a natural number, and $T(f)>0$, then
$\Theta(f,\epsilon,\eta,k)>0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Threshold power identity]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold_rpow}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.improvedFriedgutRho, FABL.improvedFriedgutRho_pos, FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean
function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ and an integer $k\ge0$, suppose the total
influence $I(f)$ is positive, where $I(f)$ is the sum over coordinates of the expected
squared discrete derivative of the real-valued sign function $f$. Then
$$\left(\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\left(\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}\right)^k\right)^{1+\eta}\right)^{1/(1+\eta)}=\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\left(\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}\right)^k.$$
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut family]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutFamily}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold, FABL.influentialCoordinates}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in
$\{−1,1\}$, and let $\epsilon,\eta\in\mathbb R$. The improved Friedgut family consists
of all finite coordinate sets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that either every
coordinate in $S$ is influential for $f$ at the improved Friedgut threshold
$\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\rho(\eta)^k\right)^{1+\eta}$, or $k<|S|$, where $I(f)$ is
the total influence and $\rho(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut small family]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgutSmallFamily}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgutSmallFamily}

For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, real parameters
$\varepsilon$ and $\eta$, and a natural number $k$, let $T$ be the improved Friedgut
threshold determined by $f$, $\varepsilon$, $\eta$, and $k$. The improved Friedgut
small family consists of all sets of coordinates $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ that are
contained in the influential coordinates of $f$ at threshold $T$ and satisfy $|S|\le k$.
\end{definition}

\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedUpTo, FABL.IsKJunta, FABL.card_improvedFriedgutCoordinates_le_general, FABL.coordinateJuntaApproximation, FABL.coordinateJuntaApproximation_isKJunta, FABL.improvedFriedgutGeneralJuntaSizeTerm, FABL.improvedFriedgutSmallFamily, FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold, FABL.improvedFriedgut_coordinateJunta_close, FABL.improvedFriedgut_small_spectrum_concentrated, FABL.influentialCoordinates, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.totalInfluence}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean
function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ and an integer $k\ge0$, suppose the total
influence $I(f)$ is positive and the sum of squared Fourier coefficients over sets of
size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$. Put $C=(2/\eta+1)^{1+\eta}$ and
$M=I(f)^{2+\eta}/(\epsilon^{1+\eta}C^k)$. There exist a coordinate set $J$ and a Boolean
function $g$ such that $|J|\le M$, the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $f$
outside the family of sets $S\subseteq J$ with $|S|\le k$ is at most $2\epsilon$, $g$
depends on at most $|J|$ coordinates, and the fraction of inputs on which $f$ and $g$
differ is at most $\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a close junta]
\lean{FABL.improvedFriedgut_exists_close_junta}
\label{FABL.improvedFriedgut_exists_close_junta}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedUpTo, FABL.IsKJunta, FABL.card_improvedFriedgutCoordinates_le, FABL.coordinateJuntaApproximation, FABL.coordinateJuntaApproximation_isKJunta, FABL.improvedFriedgutJuntaSizeTerm, FABL.improvedFriedgutSmallFamily, FABL.improvedFriedgutThreshold, FABL.improvedFriedgut_coordinateJunta_close, FABL.improvedFriedgut_small_spectrum_concentrated, FABL.influentialCoordinates, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean
function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ with $\eta\le1$ and an integer $k\ge0$,
suppose the total influence $I(f)$ is positive and the sum of squared Fourier
coefficients over sets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$. Put
$C=(2/\eta+1)^2$ and $M=I(f)^{2+\eta}/(\epsilon^{1+\eta}C^k)$. There exist a coordinate
set $J$ and a Boolean function $g$ such that $|J|\le M$, the sum of squared Fourier
coefficients of $f$ outside the family of sets $S\subseteq J$ with $|S|\le k$ is at most
$2\epsilon$, $g$ depends on at most $|J|$ coordinates, and the fraction of inputs on
which $f$ and $g$ differ is at most $\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut degree for linear threshold functions]
\lean{FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutDegree}
\label{FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutDegree}
\leanok
For a real number $\epsilon$, the improved Friedgut degree for linear threshold
functions is the least natural number greater than or equal to $16/\epsilon^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier concentration for threshold functions]
\lean{FABL.ltf_spectrum_concentrated_up_to_improvedFriedgutDegree}
\label{FABL.ltf_spectrum_concentrated_up_to_improvedFriedgutDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedUpTo, FABL.IsLinearThreshold, FABL.fourierWeightAboveReal_natCast, FABL.fourierWeightAbove_pred_le_four_div_sqrt_of_isLinearThreshold, FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutDegree}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube that is a linear
threshold function. For every $\varepsilon>0$, the sum of the squared Fourier
coefficients of its real-valued sign representation over all coordinate sets $S$ with
$|S|>\lceil16/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Improved Friedgut junta size bound]
\lean{FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutJuntaSizeBound}
\label{FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutJuntaSizeBound}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.improvedFriedgutJuntaSizeTerm, FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutDegree}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and real parameters
$\epsilon$ and $\eta$, the improved Friedgut junta size bound for linear threshold
functions is $1$ plus the improved Friedgut junta-size term for $f$, $\epsilon$, and
$\eta$, evaluated at the improved Friedgut degree $\lceil16/\epsilon^2\rceil$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Improved junta approximation for threshold functions]
\lean{FABL.ltf_improvedFriedgut_junta}
\label{FABL.ltf_improvedFriedgut_junta}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.IsKJunta, FABL.IsLinearThreshold, FABL.improvedFriedgutJuntaSizeTerm, FABL.improvedFriedgut_exists_close_junta, FABL.isKJunta_zero_of_totalInfluence_eq_zero, FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutDegree, FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutJuntaSizeBound, FABL.ltf_spectrum_concentrated_up_to_improvedFriedgutDegree, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.spectrum_concentrated_on_empty_of_totalInfluence_eq_zero, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_nonneg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube that is a linear
threshold function, and let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and $0<\eta<1/2$. There exist a
coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and a Boolean function $g$ depending on at most $|J|$
coordinates such that
\[|J|\le 1+\frac{I(f)^{2+\eta}}{\varepsilon^{1+\eta}}\left(\left(\frac{2}{\eta}+1\right)^2\right)^{\lceil16/\varepsilon^2\rceil},\]
the Fourier weight of the real-valued sign representation of $f$ on sets $S\subseteq J$
with $|S|\le\lceil16/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ is at least all but $2\varepsilon$ of its
total weight, and the relative Hamming distance between $f$ and $g$ is at most
$\varepsilon$. Here $I(f)$ is the total influence of the real-valued sign representation
of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear threshold approximation by juntas]
\lean{FABL.corollary9_31_ltf_close_to_junta}
\label{FABL.corollary9_31_ltf_close_to_junta}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsKJunta, FABL.IsLinearThreshold, FABL.ltfImprovedFriedgutJuntaSizeBound, FABL.ltf_improvedFriedgut_junta, FABL.relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a linear threshold function, and let
$0<\epsilon,\eta<1/2$. There exist a set $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a Boolean
function $g$ depending on at most $|J|$ coordinates such that $|J|\le
1+\dfrac{I(f)^{2+\eta}}{\epsilon^{1+\eta}}\left(\dfrac{2}{\eta}+1\right)^{2\lceil16/\epsilon^2\rceil}$
and the fraction of inputs on which $f$ and $g$ differ is at most $\epsilon$, where
$I(f)$ is the total influence of $f$.
\end{theorem}
